Neutrino Solution (NuSol) Module¶

The NuSol sub-package provides analytical single and double neutrino reconstruction using ellipse intersection methods. It exposes both a high-level C++ nusol class and a batch-capable CUDA/LibTorch interface (nusol_ namespace — see Neutrino Reconstruction (pyc)).

Entry Point¶

nusol_enum selects between the two reconstruction back-ends:

enum class nusol_enum¶

Selects the neutrino reconstruction algorithm.

Values:

enumerator ellipse¶

Use the analytic ellipse intersection method (arxiv:1305.1878).

enumerator conuix¶

Use the generalised n-neutrino Conuix method.

enumerator conuic¶
enumerator undefined¶

No algorithm selected.

struct nusol_t¶

Run parameters for the neutrino reconstruction.

Constrained Neutrino Solutions¶

conuix orchestrates multi-neutrino reconstruction by creating one conuic instance per lepton–b-jet pair and merging the solutions.

conuic implements the single-neutrino constrained solver. It finds the neutrino momentum that simultaneously satisfies the W-mass and top-mass constraints using the Möbius-parametrisation approach.

class conuic¶

Single b–lepton neutrino solver via Möbius / pencil-of-conics.

struct Mobius_t : public Conuix::debug¶

Möbius transform coefficients and the τ* minimiser.

The Möbius transform maps the conic pencil parameter λ to the neutrino parameter τ. Mobius_t stores the four Möbius coefficients (a, b, c, d), the eigenvalues, and the result of the τ* minimisation.

Polynomial root finders, matrix generators, low-level matrix arithmetic, and conic-section utilities used by the ellipse neutrino solver.

Core mathematical root finders and matrix operations specific to the ellipse solver.

(ellipse)

Provides functions to generate specific constraint matrices, apply rotations, and factor degenerate conics. Contains implementations of root finders used primarily to extract intersections between geometric conic objects in the parameter space.

Find the intersection points of an ellipse and a line in homogeneous coordinates.

Computes intersection points between an ellipse constraint and a line.

Parameters:

  • ellipse – 3×3 conic matrix.

  • line – 3×1 line vector.

  • pts – Output 3×2 matrix of homogeneous intersection points.

Returns:

Number of intersections found (0, 1, or 2).

int intersection_ellipses(mtx *A, mtx *B, mtx **lines, mtx **pts, mtx **sols)¶

Find the intersection points of two conics A and B.

Computes intersection points of two arbitrary ellipses A and B.

Parameters:

  • A – First conic (3×3).

  • B – Second conic (3×3).

  • lines – Output degenerate lines.

  • pts – Output intersection points.

  • sols – Output solution matrices.

Returns:

Number of solutions.

mtx *intersection_angle(mtx *H1, mtx *H2, mtx *MET, int *n_sols)¶

Compute the neutrino angle(s) satisfying the MET constraint.

Parameters:

  • H1 – First H-tilde matrix.

  • H2 – Second H-tilde matrix.

  • MET – Missing transverse momentum vector.

  • n_sols – Output: number of solutions found.

Returns:

Pointer to a matrix of solution angles.

mtx make_ellipse(mtx *H, double angle)¶

Evaluate the neutrino ellipse parametrically at angle.

Parameters:

  • H – H-tilde matrix.

  • angle – Parametric angle.

Returns:

3-vector on the ellipse.
